card.name: Just before a person's name in history
card.fires_on: Words right before a personal first name or title plus name, in local-history and genealogy prose. Typical spots are commas in lists of names, 'and' between names, 'Mrs.', 'married', and 'was'.

modes.label: Lists of people
modes.description: A comma or 'and' between names of settlers or officials, where another name comes next.
modes.example: The fund raisers were M. Kaplan<<,>> R. Kaplan and M. Fain

modes.label: Verb or title before a name
modes.description: A verb or title that is directly followed by a person's name.
modes.example: On January 2, 1854, he<< married>> Frances Sarah Brown, from the nearby village

modes.label: Inside a name or age phrase
modes.description: Partway through a name or an age phrase, where a name follows.
modes.example: recounted 65-year<<-old>> Ferhat Aktaş, a retired farmer

card.writes: It favors the start of an unusual or foreign-sounding name such as Abram, and lowers common modern English first names like Gary or Karen.
card.plain: It fires in old local-history text just before a settler's or person's name is about to be given.
